name: openreadout
description: Read raw lab-instrument files (microscopy, screening plates, electron microscopy, flow cytometry, electrophysiology, NMR, FT-IR/Raman, mass spectrometry, chromatography, plate readers, qPCR) without vendor software.
long_description: One static binary that reads lab-instrument files and returns what is in them: images, channels, pixel size, signals, spectra, plate reads and acquisition metadata; shows a preview image of the data and opens an interactive viewer of it in the chat; validates file integrity; answers the usual analysis question (chromatogram peaks, standard curves, Cq values, NMR peaks, spike features, gated counts, many-file tables joined to sample sheets); and exports to OME-TIFF, OME-Zarr, mzML, Parquet, NWB, JCAMP-DX, Allotrope ASM or RDML with read-back verification. Offline, no telemetry, never modifies the source file. Every tool is read-only except export, check with report=true, batch with output and index, which only write new files (exports are verified).

tools.name: openreadout_info
tools.description: What a file or data-set directory holds, from its headers: images, tables, traces, spectra, plate, experiment, assurance; view=full|structure|explain|format, or ask a question in words

tools.name: openreadout_check
tools.description: Integrity check: findings for truncation, missing planes or parts and bad blocks

tools.name: openreadout_compare
tools.description: Compare two files, e.g. a source and its export: metadata differences, geometry, channels and per-plane hashes

tools.name: openreadout_report
tools.description: A privacy-reviewed diagnostic bundle for a file that is refused, fails or is not validated

tools.name: openreadout_preview
tools.description: A picture of the data (image plane, composite, projection, zoomed region, trace, spectrum or plate heat map) as image content

tools.name: openreadout_stats
tools.description: Pixel statistics per channel and image: min, max, mean, std, percentiles, histogram, zero and saturated fractions; per=plane|well|field

tools.name: openreadout_trace
tools.description: One window of one sweep of a signal or 1-D spectrum in physical units: statistics, argmax_axis_value and samples

tools.name: openreadout_table
tools.description: Rows of a table (FCS events, plate reads, event, spike and peak tables); FCS optionally compensated, transformed and gated; filter and count

tools.name: openreadout_scans
tools.description: Mass-spectrometry scan headers, filtered and counted, without decoding peaks

tools.name: openreadout_spectrum
tools.description: One mass spectrum's m/z and intensity arrays, by scan number, index, or the nth scan of an MS level

tools.name: openreadout_peaks
tools.description: Chromatographic peaks with area, height, widths, tailing, plates, resolution, S/N and purity; bands and regions of spectra

tools.name: openreadout_chromatogram
tools.description: TIC, BPC, extracted-ion, SRM/MRM and detector chromatograms with apex and integral

tools.name: openreadout_nmr_peaks
tools.description: NMR peak list and region integrals, from the vendor's spectrum or the FID

tools.name: openreadout_ephys_features
tools.description: Patch-clamp features: action potentials, rheobase, f-I slope, passive properties

tools.name: openreadout_spikes
tools.description: Extracellular spike counts, rates and times per channel

tools.name: openreadout_qpcr
tools.description: qPCR results per well and target: Cq, Tm, ΔΔCq fold changes, standard curves

tools.name: openreadout_gate
tools.description: Flow-cytometry gating from a FlowJo workspace or Gating-ML file: population counts, percentages and medians

tools.name: openreadout_assay_wells
tools.description: Plate-reader wells: roles, blank subtraction, replicate statistics and outliers

tools.name: openreadout_assay_curve
tools.description: Plate-reader standard curve and back-calculated concentrations

tools.name: openreadout_dose_response
tools.description: Plate-reader dose-response: IC50/EC50 per compound

tools.name: openreadout_kinetics
tools.description: Plate-reader kinetic reads: max slope, lag time, AUC per well

tools.name: openreadout_growth
tools.description: Plate-reader growth curves: growth rate and doubling time per well

tools.name: openreadout_assay_qc
tools.description: Plate-reader assay quality: Z′, signal/background, CVs

tools.name: openreadout_export
tools.description: Convert to OME-TIFF, OME-Zarr, CSV, Parquet, mzML, NWB, JCAMP-DX, Allotrope ASM or RDML with read-back verification

tools.name: openreadout_extract
tools.description: Write an embedded attachment (slide label, thumbnail, time stamps) to a new file as stored

tools.name: openreadout_batch
tools.description: Any measure or analysis over many files as one tidy table, joined to sample sheets and summarized by group

tools.name: openreadout_summarize
tools.description: Group statistics of a saved table, with replicate averaging and tests against a control

tools.name: openreadout_link
tools.description: Group files that measured the same sample across instruments, with the evidence and a confidence

tools.name: openreadout_index
tools.description: Catalog every data set under directories into an index of Parquet tables (headers only; resumable)

tools.name: openreadout_search
tools.description: Search an index: data sets matching a query such as objective=63x channel~GFP acquired<2020

tools.name: openreadout_health
tools.description: Storage health of an indexed share: truncated or corrupt files, duplicates, files at risk

tools.name: openreadout_watch
tools.description: Watch directories where instruments write: new data sets, planes and scans, completion, stalls and live QC events since a cursor

prompts.name: summarize_file
prompts.text: Summarize the lab-instrument file ${arguments.file}: call openreadout_info (view=explain for an account in words), look at it with openreadout_preview, then report what it is, what was measured and how, when, and anything unusual. Only state values the tools returned.

prompts.name: check_file
prompts.description: Check a file and explain problems
prompts.text: Check whether ${arguments.file} is intact with openreadout_check. Explain every finding in plain language (cause, affected data) and suggest how to salvage what is readable.

prompts.name: convert_to_open_format
prompts.text: Convert ${arguments.file} to the open format that fits its data (OME-TIFF or OME-Zarr for images, mzML for mass spectra, Allotrope ASM for plate reads; CSV via the CLI for tables and traces) with openreadout_export, after checking its size with openreadout_info. Report the output path and whether it was verified.
